title: Aspect ratios explained: 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 9:16 and how to calculate — cv.cm
description: An aspect ratio is width to height, written like 16:9. See common ratios for photos, video and screens, and how to compute sizes and crop without stretching.
answer: An aspect ratio is the proportion between an image's width and its height, written as two numbers such as 16:9 or 4:3. It describes shape, not size: 1920 × 1080 and 1280 × 720 are both 16:9. To keep the ratio when resizing, compute the new height as new width × height ÷ width; for 16:9 at 1200 pixels wide, that is 675 pixels high.

head: Ratio

Example size (px)

rows: Phone camera photos, older TVs, tablets
ISO paper sizes such as A4

body: The 16:9 ratio became the HDTV standard through ITU-R BT.709, which defines 1920 × 1080 and 1280 × 720 pictures. 3:2 comes from the 36 × 24 mm frame of 35 mm film.

sections.h: How to find the ratio of any image
body: Divide width and height by their greatest common divisor (GCD).

ol: Take the pixel size, for example 1920 × 1080.
Find the largest number that divides both: 120.
Divide: 1920 ÷ 120 = 16 and 1080 ÷ 120 = 9, so the ratio is 16:9.

body: Some sizes only approximate a named ratio. A 1366 × 768 laptop screen reduces to 683:384, which is 1.779 and is sold as 16:9. A 2560 × 1080 "21:9" monitor is exactly 64:27. Comparing decimals (width ÷ height) is often easier than comparing fractions.

sections.h: Calculating a new size without distortion
body: Keep the ratio by scaling both sides by the same factor. Two formulas cover every case:

ul: `new height = new width × original height ÷ original width`
`new width = new height × original width ÷ original height`

body: Example: a 4032 × 3024 photo (4:3) resized to 1600 pixels wide becomes 1600 × 3024 ÷ 4032 = 1200 pixels high. For a 9:16 video at 720 pixels wide, the height is 720 × 16 ÷ 9 = 1280.
When the result is not a whole number, round to the nearest pixel. Video encoders usually require even dimensions, so round to an even number for video.

sections.h: Changing the ratio: crop, pad or stretch
body: Turning a 4:3 photo into a 16:9 frame or a 1:1 post cannot be done by resizing alone. There are three choices:

head: Method
What happens
When to use it
rows: Cuts away part of the image
Most photos; keep the subject inside the frame
Adds bars or a blurred background
When nothing may be cut, such as documents or art
Almost never; faces and circles look distorted

body: Cropping a 4000 × 3000 image to 16:9 keeps the full width and cuts the height to 4000 × 9 ÷ 16 = 2250 pixels, discarding 25% of the picture. Cropping the same image to 1:1 keeps 3000 × 3000.

CSS has an `aspect-ratio` property, for example `aspect-ratio: 16 / 9`, which reserves the right amount of space before an image or video loads. Setting it, or giving images `width` and `height` attributes, prevents the page from jumping as media arrives, which improves the Cumulative Layout Shift score.

body.note: Platforms change their recommended upload sizes over time. Check the current help page of the service before preparing a large batch of images or a video.

faq.a: 16:9. Both numbers divide by 120, giving 16 and 9.
Consumer 4K UHD is 3840 × 2160, exactly 16:9. Cinema 4K (DCI) is 4096 × 2160, about 1.90:1.

faq.q: What is the aspect ratio of a phone photo?
faq.a: Most phone cameras shoot 4:3 by default, such as 4032 × 3024. Many also offer 16:9 and 1:1 modes, which crop the sensor image.

faq.q: Does changing the aspect ratio reduce quality?
faq.a: Cropping removes pixels but does not blur the rest. Stretching distorts shapes, and enlarging after a heavy crop can make the image look soft.
